invariants.rule: Keep context size, model, quantization, GPU topology, and worker count unchanged while repairing Qwen turn and tool registration semantics.
Modify only local-coding-worker in the skills repository; do not bootstrap, claim, or modify Cellerator or CE-ARCH work.
Retain schema-backed structured output and fail closed when the installed Qwen lacks strict core-tool registration.
The MCP facade owns no project truth; todo, canonical source, local-worker, and CUDA retain their existing authorities.
Existing public CLIs and active project plans remain valid and unchanged.
Normal Codex context contains only bounded work, scope, evidence, outcome, and opaque handles—not skill machinery or raw tokens.
Unavailable local GPUs never block, queue, scope-lock, or reduce frontier Codex parallelism.
Never reset, clean, overwrite, or commit unrelated user work.
C4Q-01 and every C4Q-owned source or evidence path are outside PCU scope.

Cellerator is outside PCU-V1 mutation authority; only read-only Project Control observation and genuinely independent-clone rehearsal are allowed, and detected mutation is a campaign failure without automatic repair.
Downstream migration changes only owned guidance/configuration in a new ordinary commit and never rewrites history or identity.
New projects use project-control; existing coding-workflow projects remain valid during the migration window.
Existing Git and todo history remains intact and is extended only by ordinary forward commits and events.
Historical coding-workflow sessions and claims remain readable and recoverable.
PCU-V1 does not delete the compatibility package, standalone Project Control checkout, historical worktrees, stale sessions, or state files.
No Skills shim or Todo component implements a workflow operation by calling another MCP server.
Only project-control is registered as the live Codex MCP after cutover.
Candidate installation and final cutover retain an automatic restoration path.
No runtime or approval secret enters repository artifacts.
Project Control enters Skills only as a gitlink to its existing repository history.
Todo Orchestrator remains the sole workflow database, transaction, revision, scheduling, capability, and recovery authority.

Local-worker child executions remain bounded subordinates of exactly one active parent claim and are never lanes, roles, run participants, todo owners, communicators, rendezvous participants, or parent completers.
coding-workflow is the only ordinary model-facing workflow protocol; todo-orchestrator is its transactional kernel and maintenance interface.

Parallel lanes own disjoint modules and worktrees; shared service, command, schema normalization, projection, registry, and compatibility integration files are owned only by WFU-20 or later release tasks.
cpp-context-compiler, CUDA, and local-coding-worker remain bounded specialized engines; MCP startup performs no GPU, model, repository scan, or benchmark work.
Raw todo, session, child, recovery, GPU, endpoint, packet, log, and transcript secrets never cross the model-facing MCP boundary.
Project-control remains a separate stateless read-only observation plane with exactly eight public MCP tools.

Existing v2 plans, snapshots, lifecycle entities, terminal provenance, child executions, gates, leases, interfaces, decisions, evidence, and historical audit remain readable and functional through forward-only migrations.
Never reset, clean, overwrite, delete, or silently attribute user files, dirty worktrees, commits, patches, or unrelated C4Q state.
Todo SQLite is the sole live semantic authority; every mutation is transactional, revisioned, and append-only in event history.
